findings: P01-02 loss of events queued during repository dispatch

failed_cases: in-memory event bus delivery coalesces simultaneous publication until the single delivery finishes
in-memory event bus delivery shares a concurrent failure and permits a later retry without repeating successful handlers
in-memory event bus delivery uses the subscription snapshot captured before delivery
in-memory event bus delivery never evicts active delivery while settled history fills
repository pending-event dispatch preserves events added while an earlier batch is being delivered

changes: Concurrent publications of one event ID share one active attempt and its rejection/success.
Subscriber snapshots isolate active delivery from subscribe/unsubscribe operations.
Active attempts are separate from the bounded 10,000 settled-success/failure histories. Duplicate successful publication does not extend retention.
Successful repository dispatch acknowledges its captured event references only; later queued events survive. No-argument clearing and the existing missing-bus discard behavior are preserved.
coverage_scope: Only the four listed implementation files; 100% lines/statements/functions/branches. Not all core, infrastructure or backend coverage.

checks.root_tsc: passed for changed production contracts and tests
checks.postgres: 47 groups pass; actual reservation save remains committed after handler failure, pending event retained, retry leaves one persisted row, synthetic fixtures removed; final temporary DB absent

review_scope.note: Consumer snippets establish the reviewed dependency paths, not entire cart/container/module review. Core package had an earlier complete initial read.

verification_history: First implementation left one retention test failing (43 pass/1 fail); duplicate-success publication now preserves the existing eviction window. Final expanded focused suite is 45/45.
Compiler rejected a new harness comparison narrowed across an async call; explicitly capture the post-retry event-array snapshot. No application logic was changed to resolve that checker assertion.
limits: In-memory deduplication is scoped to a bus instance and handler reference. Eviction, process restart and subscriber side effects before rejection permit redelivery; this is not exactly-once or durable delivery.
Active attempts are not evicted and have no built-in timeout/cancellation/concurrency admission limit. Handlers must not await their own active event or cyclic event dependencies.
Database commit and delivery remain separate. Real PostgreSQL proves the documented failure boundary, not atomic outbox/reliable messaging or whole-cart integration.
The stock.added subscriber catches its own failures, so the bus can only treat the resolved handler as success. Existing P10 restock/simulated-provider review remains open.
Missing-bus discard behavior is retained; composition must verify required buses/subscribers are actually wired. Full file/module closure remains pending these dependent checks.
